solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bird: irrational figure in coal mine (5)

indicators.note: 'in' places the figure inside the mine, as a miner is in the pit

blocks.note: a coal mine is a pit; it opens after its first two letters
pi is the classic irrational number

annotation.surface: A strange account of a bird turning up down a coal mine, like the proverbial canary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' sounds like an insult but is exact mathematics: a number that cannot be written as a fraction. The answer's stutter is the clue that one piece sits inside the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain category definition: the pipit is a small brown songbird of fields and moors.

entries.clue: A pregnant soprano losing lead in Puccini having developed unacceptable figure (7,3,5)

indicators.note: 'losing' means going without, so soprano goes without the letter named
something that has developed has changed its form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: SOPRANO drops P, the first letter of Puccini

annotation.surface: An opera singer, expecting a baby, has grown too big for her Puccini role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead in Puccini' reads like a starring role, but it is only the letter P, which must come out of SOPRANO before the fifteen letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin diplomatic phrase: a persona non grata is a person no longer welcome, so an unacceptable figure.

entries.clue: Trial scheme bringing in electric current (5)

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the scheme takes the current inside it

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for current

annotation.surface: A trial scheme to connect some district to the electricity supply.
annotation.walkthrough: I for current is standard physics notation and a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: Pilot is used as an adjective here, as in a pilot scheme: a small trial run before the real thing.

entries.clue: Tense? My rising alarm shuts out constant sources of drumming (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from the bottom upwards
to shut someone out is to exclude them, so the constant is excluded from alarm

blocks.note: PANIC without C, the symbol for a constant (and the speed of light)

annotation.surface: A nervous waker rising to an alarm, with the constant thud of drums in the background.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense?' looks like a question about nerves; it is just T. The definition is plural because tympani are a set of kettledrums.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: tympani (timpani) are the orchestra's kettledrums, the instruments that produce the drumming.

entries.clue: Stretch limo shortened it to make deadline (4,5)

indicators.note: a word that is shortened is made less long, so limo loses its last letter

blocks.note: a stretch is time served in prison

annotation.surface: A chauffeur trims a stretch limo so it can beat a deadline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stretch limo' is a single phrase in the surface; split it, and stretch is a prison sentence, which is time.
annotation.definitionFit: A close synonym: a deadline is the point by which work must be done, the time allowed running out.

entries.clue: Considerable trouble in darkest Yorkshire at the outset (4)

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

annotation.surface: Someone warns of considerable trouble in the gloomy depths of Yorkshire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Considerable' feels far from neatness, but tidy has a second, informal sense of large.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British sense: a tidy sum is a considerable one.

entries.clue: Obstinate type trimmed US magazine to help rising use of many information outlets (10)

indicators.note: trimming cuts a little off the end, so mule loses its last letter
in a down clue a word that rises is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a mule is an obstinate type; drop its last letter

annotation.surface: A stubborn editor cuts back an American magazine to push it into new media.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive phrase rather than a synonym; 'information outlets' are simply media.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: multimedia means combining many media, text, sound, video, in one presentation.

entries.clue: Scoundrel losing head in American city opera house (2,5)

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, so losing it removes that letter
'in' places the shortened word inside the city's letters

annotation.surface: A villain loses his head at an American opera house.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places the opera house in America; La Scala is in Milan, and LA merely wraps around the rascal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: La Scala in Milan is one of the world's most famous opera houses.

entries.clue: Man penning newspaper’s last stories about French city (9)

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as sheep in a pen, so man encloses the rest
a word's last is its final letter
'about' as in turned about, so the stories face the other way

blocks.note: a man is a male; it opens after MA

annotation.surface: A journalist writing up the final stories of a newspaper about a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stories' are lies, as in telling stories to cover up. 'Penning' pretends to mean writing, which suits the newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Marseille is France's great Mediterranean port.

entries.clue: Astonished and attracted to almost certain start of presidential revolt (5,2,8)

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the word stops one letter short
a word's start is its first letter

blocks.note: to rise up is to revolt

annotation.surface: Shocked but drawn to the near-certain start of a revolt against the president.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces fall out almost word for word, the trick being to hear 'attracted to' as 'taken by'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone caught unawares by the unexpected is astonished.

entries.clue: Electronic form in register is a good example (4,5)

indicators.note: 'in' places the form inside the register, as an entry sits in a book

blocks.note: a roll is a register of names; it opens after ROL
a mode is a form or manner

annotation.surface: An electronic form filed in the register counts as a good example.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like office paperwork; 'Electronic form' must split into E and MODE.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a role model is a person others copy because they set a good example.

entries.clue: Film franchise? I will avoid Scream (5)

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so I keeps out of the scream

annotation.surface: A film franchise named, and someone vowing not to watch Scream, the horror series.
annotation.walkthrough: Scream is itself a horror film franchise, so the capital S pulls the eye away from the plain verb shriek.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shrek is the animated ogre film series with several sequels.

entries.clue: Expense from parts of arrangement being switched? (6)

indicators.note: things that are switched swap places, so the two halves change round

blocks.note: a layout is an arrangement, made of the parts LAY and OUT

annotation.surface: A cost arising because parts of some arrangement were swapped over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' tells you the arrangement word is built from two smaller words, and 'switched' swaps them; the question mark flags that the definition comes by an unusual route.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outlay is money laid out, an expense.

entries.clue: Branch bearing a half-Andean vegetable (4,4)

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the branch carries A inside it
half of a word is used, here its second half

blocks.note: a limb is a branch of a tree; it opens after LIM

annotation.surface: A branch hung with a vegetable that is half from the Andes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: the lima bean is named after Lima, Peru's capital, so it really is Andean.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lima bean is a pale, flat bean eaten as a vegetable.

entries.clue: Branch of medicine that could make you stay chirpy (10)

indicators.note: the letters could make, that is be rearranged into, the answer

annotation.surface: A branch of medicine that promises to keep you cheerful.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a description of the answer, since psychiatry aims to keep patients well in mind.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: psychiatry is the medical specialty treating mental illness.

entries.clue: Agree cops should release head of Roman church (9)

indicators.note: to release is to let go, so ACQUIRES lets go of a letter
a word's head is its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: cops should release head of Roman
blocks.note: cops = acquires (gets); ACQUIRES loses R, the first letter of Roman

annotation.surface: An appeal for the police to free a leading Roman churchman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cops' looks like the police but is the verb, as in 'cops a fine': ACQUIRES, which then drops R.
annotation.definitionFit: A close synonym: to acquiesce is to agree, usually quietly or reluctantly.

entries.clue: Question over description of sea omitting one island in equation (9)

indicators.note: to omit is to leave out, so the letter is left out

blocks.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question

blocks.clueFragment: description of sea omitting one island
blocks.note: ADRIATIC, which describes a sea, without I (one island: I is both one and island)

annotation.surface: A puzzle set over a map of the sea, leaving out one island.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts QU above the rest. Adriatic is the adjective in 'the Adriatic Sea', hence 'description of sea'.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a quadratic is an equation in which the unknown is squared.

entries.clue: Mixture of everything two-thirds of crossword solvers recalled (5)

indicators.note: two-thirds of a three-letter word is its first two letters
to recall is to call back, so the letters come back the other way

blocks.note: crossword solvers are YOU; two-thirds is YO, turned round

annotation.surface: A mixture of everything that most solvers can recall.
annotation.walkthrough: Setters address solvers as 'you', so 'crossword solvers' is YOU.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: an alloy is a metal made by mixing two or more metals.

entries.clue: Acceptable area to house South African in Japanese city (5)

indicators.note: to house someone is to give them a home inside, so the outer letters hold the South African

blocks.note: OK = acceptable; it opens after O

annotation.surface: A suitable district to house a South African living in a Japanese city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acceptable area' reads as one estate agent's phrase; it is two pieces that between them make the wrapper.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Osaka is Japan's big commercial city on Honshu.

entries.clue: Supply heater’s source of wood (3,4)

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, in a bending way, so the letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters with the S

annotation.surface: An instruction to supply a heater with its fuel of wood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as the verb provide; here it is the adverb from supple, so the letters bend.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the ash tree is a common source of timber and firewood.

entries.clue: Cut deal with university after money and drink (9)

indicators.note: a cut word is trimmed, so treat loses its last letter
'after' puts these pieces behind the money

blocks.note: to treat is to deal with; cut its last letter

annotation.surface: A cut-price deal with a university, sweetened by money and drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deal with' is one idea, TREAT; 'Cut deal' looks like a phrase on its own and must be split differently.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur.

entries.clue: Flaxen fibres gently touch hard walking surface (7)

blocks.note: tow is the coarse fibre of flax or hemp
to pat is to touch gently

annotation.surface: Flax fibres lightly brushing a hard path underfoot.
annotation.walkthrough: Tow is a less familiar word: the short coarse fibres left from processing flax.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a towpath runs beside a canal, where horses once towed barges, and is now walked.

entries.clue: Composer, German, with quiet success (8)

annotation.surface: A composer, German by birth, enjoying quiet success.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a German composer, but Gershwin was American.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: George Gershwin wrote Rhapsody in Blue.

entries.clue: Just appear pale, in the grip of drink (4,2)

indicators.note: something held in a grip is enclosed, so drink holds pale inside it

blocks.note: to sup is to drink; it opens after S

annotation.surface: Someone who looks pale and seems to be in the grip of drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' carries the sense of the phrase: to swan up is to turn up casually, as if without a care.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal idiom: to swan up is to arrive nonchalantly, simply to appear.

entries.clue: Radiant, unconfined free spirit (5)

indicators.note: the outer letters are the confining walls, so removing them leaves the word unconfined
letters set free are no longer held in their order

blocks.note: RADIANT without its outer letters R and T

annotation.surface: A radiant free spirit, not confined by anything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free spirit' reads as one phrase, but 'free' is the anagram signal and 'spirit' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a spirit of rivers and springs.

entries.clue: I fish, letting nothing escape is key (4)

indicators.note: letting means allowing, so the fish allows the letter out
what escapes gets out, so O leaves the fish

annotation.surface: An angler boasting that no fish ever gets away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' is a low island, as in the Florida Keys, not a thing for a lock.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: a key or cay is a small low island, an isle.

entries.clue: A lot of maps moving westward end of water table (5)

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so one letter goes
on a map west is to the left, so in an across clue the word runs backwards
a word's end is its last letter

blocks.clueFragment: A lot of maps moving westward
blocks.note: maps = ATLAS; most of it is ATLA, reversed

annotation.surface: Most of a set of maps drifting west until the water table runs out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Water table' is a single geological phrase in the surface; it splits, and only 'table' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: the altar is the communion table in a church.

entries.clue: Italian maestro’s Italian opera: popular, repeatedly returning (9)

indicators.note: done repeatedly means done more than once, so the word is used twice
coming back means going the other way, so each copy is reversed

annotation.surface: An Italian conductor's favourite opera, a hit that keeps coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay. The two 'Italian's are separate words: one in the definition, one describing the opera.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arturo Toscanini was the great Italian conductor, and maestro is the title for one.

entries.clue: Cheap tyre burst, for example (9)

indicators.note: a burst tyre flies apart, and so do its letters

annotation.surface: A cheap tyre that blew out, held up as a warning example.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For example' reads as a stock phrase; split it, and 'for' links while 'example' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A close synonym: an archetype is the original or model example of which others are copies.

entries.clue: Start of hundred inch garden feature? (5)

indicators.note: a word's start is its first letter

blocks.note: to inch is to edge forward slowly

annotation.surface: A garden feature starting at a hundred inches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a measurement to go with 'hundred', but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a hedge is a row of bushes forming a garden boundary.
